passage:
Shreya: are you awake
Jasleen: yes. how are you both?
Shreya: baby's asleep. i'm crying because my tea went cold
Shreya: and because i love her so much it hurts, and i'm so tired i can't think
Jasleen: oh Shreya. that sounds so hard
Shreya: everyone keeps saying these are the happiest days. what's wrong with me
Jasleen: nothing. your body has just done something huge and you've barely slept
Jasleen: lots of new mums feel exactly this in the first days
Shreya: really?
Jasleen: really, didi. i'm coming tomorrow morning with dal and rotis. i'll hold her, you sleep
Shreya: you'd do that?
Jasleen: already packing. and if it keeps going or worries you, we'll call your doctor together
Shreya: ok. thank you
Jasleen: drink some water and try to rest when she does

qa.q: What made Shreya cry, according to her message?
qa.a: Her tea went cold.

qa.q: What was Shreya feeling in these messages?
qa.a: She felt overwhelmed, exhausted and tearful, loving the baby intensely while worrying something was wrong with her.

qa.q: What practical help does Jasleen offer, and why does it matter?
qa.a: Coming with dal and rotis and holding the baby so Shreya can sleep; rest, food and reassurance often ease these early days.

qa.q: How does Jasleen seem to read Shreya's tears?
qa.a: Jasleen sees them as a common response to a huge change and little sleep, not as something wrong with Shreya.

grounding: Shows a new mother crying easily and feeling overwhelmed in the first days after birth, and rest, food, reassurance and practical help easing it.

passage: A few days after Geeta came home from the health centre with the baby, she started crying at everything: a spilled glass, a kind word, the sound of the pressure cooker. In their village near Mandi, Kamal's mother frowned. "Why cry? You have a healthy son." Geeta cried harder. That evening her brother Pradeep arrived on the bus with a tiffin of their mother's rajma and sat by her cot. "Didi, you've hardly slept. Anyone would cry." Kamal listened. From that night he took the baby between feeds, walking him up and down the courtyard so Geeta could sleep. Pradeep stayed two days, washing clothes and making her eat. "If it keeps going or worries you, we'll see the doctor at the health centre," Kamal told her. Slowly, as the nights got easier, so did the tears.

qa.q: What did Pradeep bring on the bus?
qa.a: A tiffin of their mother's rajma.

qa.q: How did Geeta feel when Kamal's mother asked why she was crying?
qa.a: She felt misunderstood and even more overwhelmed, so she cried harder.

qa.q: What helped Geeta, and why?
qa.a: Kamal walking the baby between feeds so she could sleep, and Pradeep bringing food and doing chores; rest, food and reassurance ease these early days.

qa.q: How does Pradeep see his sister's tears?
qa.a: He sees them as a natural result of exhaustion, not ingratitude, and says anyone would cry.

grounding: Illustrates a new mother crying easily and feeling overwhelmed after birth, and rest, food, reassurance and practical help from family easing it.

passage:
Day 3: Home from the hospital in Nagpur, Sakshi cried because the baby's cap was crooked, then because she had been happy a minute ago, then because she couldn't stop. She hadn't slept more than an hour at a stretch. Pranav hovered, frightened, asking what was wrong.
Day 5: Sakshi's mother moved into the spare room. Pranav took two of the night feeds with expressed milk so Sakshi could sleep. Her mother brought her hot food and sat with her. Sakshi still teared up at a lullaby, but she laughed at Pranav's attempts at nappies.
Day 12: The tears came less often. At the check-up Sakshi told the nurse about the crying days, and the nurse said it was common and to tell her if it kept going or got worse. That evening Sakshi sat on the balcony with the baby asleep on her chest and felt, mostly, like herself.

qa.q: Who moved into the spare room?
qa.a: Sakshi's mother.

qa.q: What was Sakshi feeling on day 3?
qa.a: She felt overwhelmed and unusually sensitive, crying at small things and unable to stop, with almost no sleep.

qa.q: What helped Sakshi by day 12?
qa.a: Rest while Pranav took night feeds, hot food and company from her mother, and telling the nurse, who asked to hear if it kept going.

qa.q: How did Pranav feel on day 3?
qa.a: He was frightened and unsure, hovering and asking what was wrong.

grounding: Shows a new mother crying easily and feeling overwhelmed in the first days after birth, and rest, food, reassurance and practical help easing it.

passage: Anand, you rang me at midnight because Priya cried all evening and you don't know what's wrong. Listen to your old Joseph Appachan. When your mother was born, in our house in Kottayam, your Ammachi, Mary, cried for days. She cried when the milk came in, cried when the neighbours visited, cried because the baby was beautiful. I was twenty-six and useless; I thought I had done something wrong. My own mother said, "Joseph, she's worn out and her body is changing back. Feed her, let her sleep, and hold the baby." So I did. I rocked your mother through the nights and brought Mary rice kanji and fish curry. My mother told her every morning, "You're doing well." Slowly Mary came back to herself. So bring Priya food, take the baby at night, and tell her she's doing well. And if the sadness stays or grows, take her to the doctor without delay.

qa.q: What did Joseph bring Mary?
qa.a: Rice kanji and fish curry.

qa.q: How did young Mary feel after the birth?
qa.a: She was overwhelmed and unusually tearful, crying at the milk coming in, at visitors and even at the baby's beauty.

qa.q: What turned things around for Mary?
qa.a: Joseph following his mother's advice: feeding Mary, letting her sleep, rocking the baby at night, and daily reassurance.

qa.q: How did young Joseph feel during those days?
qa.a: He felt useless and worried that he had done something wrong.

grounding: Shows a new mother tearful and overwhelmed in the days after birth, and food, rest, reassurance and practical help easing it.

passage: Five days after the birth, Gautam's company called him back to Pune for an audit, the power kept cutting out in the Jabalpur heat, and Tanvi was alone with the baby for the first time. By afternoon she was sitting on the floor beside the cradle, crying because the fan had stopped, because the baby had hiccups, because she didn't know why she was crying. She had slept perhaps three hours in two days. She almost didn't call anyone; she didn't want to seem weak. Then she rang her brother Tarun, who lived ten minutes away. He came with a bag of food and his wife, took the baby into the cooler room, and told Tanvi to sleep. When she woke at seven, there was dal and rice on the table and the baby was asleep. She still felt fragile. She phoned Gautam and said calmly, "I need you home by Friday."

qa.q: Why was Gautam called back to Pune?
qa.a: For an audit.

qa.q: What was Tanvi feeling on the floor beside the cradle?
qa.a: She was overwhelmed and tearful, crying at small things without knowing why, and exhausted.

qa.q: What made the difference that evening?
qa.a: Calling Tarun for practical help, so she could eat and sleep, and then asking Gautam to come home.

qa.q: How might Tarun feel on getting her call?
qa.a: He was probably concerned and glad she called, coming at once with food.

grounding: Shows a new mother crying easily and overwhelmed in the first days after birth, and food, sleep and practical help beginning to ease it.

passage: Five days after the baby came home to their Pune flat, Mehak cried because the dal was too salty. Then she cried because the baby looked so perfect. At three in the morning she cried because she couldn't remember when she'd last slept. 'I'm meant to be happy. What's wrong with me?' she sobbed to her sister Reena, who had come to stay. Reena took the baby. 'Nothing's wrong with you. Your body's been through a storm and you haven't slept. Eat this, then sleep. I'll wake you for the feed.' Reena cooked, did the laundry and fielded visitors. Slowly Mehak laughed more. 'And if the heaviness doesn't lift, or it worries you, we tell the doctor,' Reena said. Mehak nodded.

qa.q: Why did Mehak cry about the dal?
qa.a: It was too salty.

qa.q: What was Mehak worried about when she sobbed to Reena?
qa.a: She was worried something was wrong with her because she felt tearful and overwhelmed instead of simply happy.

qa.q: What practical help did Reena give?
qa.a: She took the baby so Mehak could eat and sleep, cooked, did laundry and handled visitors, and agreed they'd tell the doctor if it didn't lift.

qa.q: How might Reena have felt seeing her sister cry at three in the morning?
qa.a: Reena probably felt tender and protective, wanting to take the load so Mehak could rest.

grounding: A new mother cries easily and feels overwhelmed in the first days after birth, and rest, food, reassurance and help ease it.
